the following topics: (i) the physics of magnetized accretion flows around supermassive black holes; (ii) the physics of jet launching from the innermost regions of accretion disks; (iii) polarized emission of magnetized relativistic plasma; (iv) application of the model to observations of the M 87 galaxy core.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
M87 jet launching region has an accretion rate of ~0.01 M_sun yr^-1 and the jet power is ~10^45 erg/s.
the mass accretions rate of the M87 black hole is 1/3 to 1/4 of the Eddington limit.
our model of the jet launching zone in M87 is consistent with the observational data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the polarized emission and Faraday rotation in the M87 jet core can be explained by a model of a magnetically driven outflow from an accretion flow with a moderate mass accretion of 0.01 M _{solar} yr ^{−1}.
the observed rotation measure and the polarized emission of the M87 core can be explained by the jet model, if the mass accreted onto the M87 black hole is less than 0.1 of the Eddington rate.
our models are in agreement with the observations and can be used for the interpretation of the M87 radio jet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polarized emission is produced in the jet launching region and the jet itself.
the polarized emission and the rotation measure in the M87 jet are consistent with the presence of the magnetized Advection dominated accretion flow in the M87 nucleus.
the observed low radio polarization of M87 core can be explained by a combination of the Faraday depolarization in the accretion flow and the jet.
